_about: Systems the plans' keynotes build (keynotes.rs, the guided job's keynote step): a system's names as notes and schedules write them, and the parts of it the job must find in the documents before it builds or prices them. A part no document places stays `undecided`, with why; it is never guessed.

systems.name: BDA
systems.title: emergency responder radio coverage (BDA)
systems.source: IFC 510 and NFPA 1221 (emergency responder radio coverage): a head-end (bi-directional amplifier, on a dedicated circuit with standby power), a donor antenna outside (usually the roof) and the coverage antennas inside

parts.what: the head-end (bi-directional amplifier) and its power
the donor antenna and its cable to the head-end

unpowered_boxes.source: trade practice: a system's antenna box holds its antenna's mount and cable, low-voltage only; no branch circuit lands in it (the system's power is its head-end's, on its own circuit)

equipment_receptacle._about: A keynote that calls for a receptacle for a piece of equipment (`30A/2P RECEPTACLE FOR <unit>, SET HORIZONTALLY IN ITS SUB-BASE`): the receptacle at its marker takes the note's rating, poles, orientation and place, and it is that equipment's connection, its only one (keynotes.rs `equipment_receptacle`, the guided job's typical rooms). The equipment's names are the rules data's own (`equipment.room_unit_tags`, `equipment.typical_load_words` in wordrules.json).
equipment_receptacle.source: the documents' keynote first; trade practice for what the note leaves out
equipment_receptacle.sub_base_source: trade practice: a packaged unit's electrical sub-base is a few inches high (makers' sub-bases are about 3-1/2 to 4 in); the unit sits on it and its receptacle is set in it, under the unit
equipment_receptacle.nema_source: NEMA WD 6 (straight-blade configurations): a 2-pole 3-wire grounding receptacle, no neutral, is the 6- family (250 V); a 1-pole one with its neutral the 5- family (125 V)

device_requirements._about: A keynote that sets a device's type, features, ganging, mounting or pathway is answered at its marker: the device its marker points at takes what it asks, the keynote its source (keynotes.rs `device_requirements`, the guided job's typical rooms and keynote step). A note that names a kind of device in some rooms (`ALL <rooms> RECEPTACLES SHALL BE …`) applies to every such device in rooms so named, building-wide. Each list below is the words the trades write it with.
device_requirements.source: the documents' keynote at its marker; the words as the trades write them
device_requirements.features_why: a feature's words are taken longest first and once (USB-C is not also a plain USB port)
device_requirements.gang_source: the keynote at its marker: the devices it points at share one box and one plate, however far apart the plan draws their symbols (power and low-voltage still never share one: NEC 800.133(A))
device_requirements.lv_source: the keynote at its marker gives that outlet's low-voltage conduit size: it governs over a general pathway note for the outlet it points at
